**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pin the replacement Vertex model to global**

When `VERTEX_REGION` or `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` is set to a non-global location, choosing this replacement writes `vertex:gemini-3.1-pro-preview` without `config.region`, because the global-region branch below only recognizes `GEMINI_FLASH_MODELS`. `GoogleAuthManager.resolveRegion()` gives those environment variables priority over the model's entry in `VERTEX_GLOBAL_DEFAULT_MODELS`, so users whose configured location does not serve this preview get a failing generated target instead of the safe global endpoint; include this ID in the branch that emits `region: 'global'`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Document the changed Vertex target in the red-team guide**

`redteam init` now replaces Gemini 2.5 Pro with Gemini 3.1 Pro and writes an explicit global region, but this commit does not update any matching page under `site/docs/red-team/`. The scoped `src/redteam/AGENTS.md` requires documentation updates when generated configuration changes. Update the initialization or configuration guide to explain the replacement and pinned global endpoint, including that saved configurations retain their original target IDs, so users can distinguish the new initialization behavior from a migration of existing configurations.

AGENTS.md reference: [src/redteam/AGENTS.md:L52-L53](https://github.com/promptfoo/promptfoo/blob/278c80a74a6bfe274d1a8f786715183c6d3b69f7/src/redteam/AGENTS.md#L52-L53)

Thanks for this. I checked the premise against live Vertex and pushed two commits.

**What I verified**
- `gemini-2.5-pro` is gone on Vertex. A raw `generateContent` call from a project with access returns `404 NOT_FOUND` on `global`, `us-central1`, `us`, and `europe-west4`. Google's [Vertex lifecycle table](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/model-versions) lists its retirement as October 20, 2026. (The Gemini API is a separate case: there it redirects to `gemini-3.8-flash` on December 1, 2026.)
- `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` is a sound replacement. The Gemini API has announced no shutdown date for it. On Vertex it serves **only on `global`**: it returned 200 there and 404 on `us-central1`, `us`, and `europe-west4`, which matches Google's locations table. That confirms the Codex finding. Without `config.region`, a user whose `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` is `us-central1` gets a generated target that 404s. I ran the real `VertexChatProvider` with `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=us-central1`: the bare ID went to `us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com` and returned 404, and the same ID with `region: global` answered "130".

**Pushed**
- `135a5547d9`: merged current `main` (which includes #12416, the Gemini 4 picker change). I resolved the `test/onboarding.test.ts` conflict onto main's shared `GOOGLE_ONBOARDING_MODELS` list and removed the retired ID from it.
- `278c80a74a`: `redteam init` now writes `region: global` for any Vertex target whose provider default region is `global` (via `getVertexModelDefaultRegion`), so it includes the new 3.1 Pro entry. `promptfoo init` writes the existing 3.1 Pro entry with `region: global` as well. I also added a web UI test showing saved `vertex:gemini-2.5-pro` configs still resolve while the picker list no longer offers the model.

**Checks**
Focused tests fail without the source change and pass with it. The full backend suite passes (1102 files), as do `tsc`, `build`, `knip`, `architecture:check`, Biome, and the redteam setup app tests.

Not changed here: `site/docs/providers/vertex.md` still lists `vertex:gemini-2.5-pro` and uses it in two config examples. That is a separate docs cleanup.
